preamble: In six clues their wordplay element contains surplus letters, to be ignored. In a further six clues more recent versions of each of these six letters are lacking from their wordplay.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: False piece of glass picked up, something sparkling

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the words before are taken by ear, not by spelling

parts.note: false is SHAM and a piece of glass is a PANE; said together they make the answer

explanation.surface: Someone holds a fake shard of glass that catches the light and sparkles.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM PANE said aloud is CHAMPAGNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the best-known sparkling wine, so it is a fair example of something that fizzes.

clue.text: Ocean's visor lifted now and again here?

indicators.note: letters taken only every so often means every second one is picked out

parts.note: the even letters of these words
the letter missing from this wordplay, the Roman form of nu, which the preamble says must be restored

explanation.surface: A heist in an Ocean's film, where a visor is lifted now and then by someone in the gang.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the six clues missing a letter: the wordplay gives CASIO, and the N (Roman form of the Greek nu) goes back in to make CASINO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ocean's Eleven films are robberies of a Las Vegas gambling house, so 'here' points to that venue.

clue.text: Robotic mind honoured fundamental law

parts.note: artificial intelligence, a machine's mind
the missing letter, the Roman form of chi, restored inside as the preamble directs
Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An android's brain held in high regard as a basic rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay alone gives AIOM; the preamble's missing X (Roman form of chi) completes it. OM is the Order of Merit, an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth taken as a starting principle, a basic law of reasoning.

clue.text: Bills to secure banker from Santander seats

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: bills stuck on walls are posters
a banker in crosswords is a river, and Spanish for river is rio

explanation.surface: Bills drawn up to lock in a Spanish bank's employee.
explanation.walkthrough: Santander looks like the bank, but it stands for Spanish, and a 'banker' is a river (it has banks).
explanation.definitionFit: Seats is a polite word for backsides, which posteriors means.

clue.text: Kind of felt negligee on the counter

indicators.note: counter means going against the usual direction, so the letters run the other way
the answer is made of part of the next words, drawn from inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Shopping talk about the texture of a negligee laid out on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of felt' reads as a type of fabric, but 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and gentle are both adjectives for a mild, tender, considerate nature.

clue.text: Individual likely to suffer when playing a team? Yes!

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone player facing a whole team is surely going to lose, and the clue cheers its own observation.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy meat is an idiom for a person who is easily beaten or taken advantage of.

clue.text: Nice word provided theme

parts.note: the French for word, as spoken in Nice
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A pleasant word, if offered, could set the theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective pleasant, but it is the French city, so the word is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or pattern in a work, essentially a theme.

clue.text: See 14
They arrange dates by ingesting some cocaine

indicators.note: something ingesting another takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: as in multiplication: three by four is three times four
a line is a dose of the drug laid out to snort

explanation.surface: Party planners who set up dates while taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Timelines set events out in chronological order, so they arrange dates in sequence.

clue.text: Form group detained more than once, holding up lesson

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so a piece sits between the others

parts.note: with the surplus Greek eta ignored this reads dined, which is fed

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: religious education, a school lesson
a second word for dined, as the dining is done twice

explanation.surface: A group was held repeatedly, which delayed a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detained' hides the Greek letter eta; ignore it and the word is 'dined', which the clue uses twice over, with two different synonyms, around the reversed lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite into a federation, forming a single group or league.

clue.text: Junior family member boxes kissers for dons

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a son is a younger member of the family
kisser is slang for mouth, so lips

explanation.surface: A child punches people's faces in place of university teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university lecturers, but it is the verb meaning puts on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothing is to put it on, which is what slips on means for a garment.

clue.text: Cast from The Beach, perhaps, had a casual read-through

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flat stones thrown from the shore are made to bounce over the water
second meaning: glanced quickly over a text

explanation.surface: The actors of the film The Beach had a quick first read of their script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' and 'The Beach' look like a film's actors; the first half is about throwing stones that bounce off the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both throwing a stone to bounce off water and reading a text superficially.

clue.text: Nude pole-dancing Chameleon?

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the missing letter, the Roman form of mu, restored in both places as the preamble directs

explanation.surface: A colour-changing lizard performing a pole dance without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The first of the clues missing a letter: the anagram needs two Ms that the clue never supplies. Chameleon is this setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Chameleon is the name this setter writes under, so it is an example of a pen name.

clue.text: Obscure publisher's promotion giving away half its books

indicators.note: the word has two of the letter for books, and giving away half of them drops one

parts.note: the promotional text on a book's cover

explanation.surface: An obscure publisher's sales push loses half of its titles.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the standard abbreviation for book, so 'half its books' is one of the two Bs.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to make it unclear, which is what blurring it does.

clue.text: Leaving number two inside, poorly sponged

indicators.note: inside places a piece within the rest
something in a poor state is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
two of the Roman numeral one
the missing letter, the Roman form of tau, restored as the preamble directs

explanation.surface: A lavatory joke: someone leaves a number two behind after a poor clean-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is short of a T, one of the six missing Roman letters. 'Number two' is toilet humour, but it gives two Is.
explanation.definitionFit: Depositing something means putting it down and leaving it, as in leaving goods with a bank.

clue.text: Tibetan ascetic's leader: 'I'm all excited about international post'

parts.note: with the surplus Greek beta ignored this reads tin, chemical symbol SN

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
excited letters are stirred up and jumbled into a fresh order
the leader of a word is the letter at its head

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The head of a Tibetan monastery thrilled to receive mail from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: TIBETAN hides the Greek letter BETA; ignore it and TIN is left, chemical symbol SN.
explanation.definitionFit: Snail mail is the jokey name for letters sent through the postal service, slow next to email.

clue.text: Evacuation caused by damaged smoke detector

definitions.text: Evacuation caused by damaged smoke detector

parts.words: Evacuation caused by damaged smoke detector
parts.note: surface reading: a building cleared because a faulty smoke alarm went off
setter's reading: the organ that smells smoke is injured and blood drains from it

explanation.surface: A building emptied after a faulty smoke alarm sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Evacuation means draining, and the smoke detector is the part of the face that smells.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebleed is blood escaping from the nostrils, often after the organ is struck or injured.

clue.text: Fruit mushed with certain consonants in Spooner's gob

indicators.note: said by Spooner, the don famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: nasal consonants such as m and n are sounded through the nose; Spooner gives this word the other word's opening h
with the surplus Greek mu ignored this reads shed, a hut, which takes the n of the first word

explanation.surface: Fruit squashed in someone's mouth along with some consonant sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSHED hides the Greek letter MU; ignore it and SHED is left. Swap the first sounds of NASAL HUT and you say HAZEL NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazelnut is the nut of the hazel tree; botanically a nut is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Flat monument gets a new character on top

indicators.text: gets a new character on top
indicators.note: a fresh letter replaces the topmost one, which in a down entry is the first

parts.note: with the surplus Greek nu ignored this reads moment, a point in time

explanation.surface: A level memorial is given a new letter on its inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: MONUMENT hides the Greek letter NU; without it the word is MOMENT, which is JUNCTURE, and P replaces its J.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a tyre that has lost its air, which a puncture causes; the two are used as synonyms.

clue.text: Biblical father enters the outskirts of Kabul — a religious tradition

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters
Aramaic for father, used in the New Testament
taken as written
the missing letter, the Roman form of eta, restored as the preamble directs

explanation.surface: An Old Testament patriarch arrives on the edge of the Afghan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives KABBALA, a real alternative spelling, and the preamble's missing H completes the grid form.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kabbalah is the Jewish mystical tradition of interpreting scripture.

clue.text: Opposing current university rates, MP revolts

parts.note: the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: a revolt overturns order, so the letters are turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A member of parliament rebels against a university's current fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposing current' looks like protest against something present; it means against the flow of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstream means moving against the flow of a river, towards its source.

clue.text: Kind of god some minotaur seizes

indicators.note: some means only part, so a stretch is taken from the following words and the rest dropped

parts.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A mythical monster grabs hold of some type of deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters spanning the two words contains the Greek letter TAU, a surplus to be ignored, which leaves NORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse gods such as Odin and Thor form the pantheon of Scandinavian mythology.

clue.text: Shift uncomfortably large sums of money after US lawyer loses case

parts.note: the title American attorneys use after their names

explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a lawsuit; here it means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm is to wriggle or fidget from embarrassment or discomfort.

clue.text: Holy book addendum banishing the question of doubts

parts.note: a postscript added to a letter

indicators.note: banishing sends something away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: misgivings
the standard abbreviation for question

explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms form a book of the Old Testament, a collection of sacred songs.

clue.text: Power line for telephone

parts.note: a line of people waiting

explanation.walkthrough: A queue is a line of waiting people; it sounds like CUE, and the missing B goes inside.

clue.text: the world, characters inside pubs abandon promises to get round

to quit is to give up

explanation.walkthrough: The published clue begins 'Across the world', which is the definition; this copy drops 'Across'. 'Round' looks like drinks, but here it means surrounding.

clue.text: Poppy product's opening triad is lifted from heavy metal

clue.text: Meetings with the Opposition where you must give some ground
